summary.best_for: High-impact marketing and product pages that still need restraint
summary.short_read: Best overall. GPT-Taste supplied drama, frontend-skill restrained it, and frontend-design pushed the concepts beyond the generic.

summary.best_for: Balanced product suites and operational UI with strong visual identity
summary.short_read: Best no-GPT-Taste combo. Strong dashboard discipline, cohesive suite pages, and memorable enough brand/product work.

summary.best_for: Distinctive page concepts and cohesive visual systems
summary.short_read: Still the strongest single skill. It commits to memorable art direction without losing content.

summary.best_for: Expressive pages that need fewer conflicting implementation constraints
summary.short_read: A very good pair: expressive, coherent, and less over-directed than the all-four combination.

summary.best_for: Broad all-purpose coverage when consistency matters more than a single sharp direction
summary.short_read: The all-four profile is strong, but it did not win. The guidance sometimes competes and creates a slightly blended output.

summary.best_for: Balanced marketing pages where expressive composition needs restraint
summary.short_read: The original combo remains solid: much better controlled than GPT-Taste alone.

summary.best_for: Dashboards and practical multi-page product UI
summary.short_read: Strongest pair for utility surfaces, though less visually memorable on brand work.

summary.best_for: Dense product flows that still need a bolder first impression
summary.short_read: Very competent, but the added design-taste constraints make it calmer rather than clearly better than the original pair.

summary.best_for: Operational pages with a more distinctive visual wrapper
summary.short_read: Good blend of structure and character, but the dashboard became a little sparse.
Improves GPT-Taste's utility discipline, but not enough to beat the pairings that include frontend-design.
Strong first impressions, but more prone to huge type and weaker dashboard ergonomics.
Still the best single skill for dashboards, but not as strong on marketing/product memorability.
Interesting but uneven. It sometimes becomes more editorial than useful.
Reliable and polished, but safer than the best combinations.
Memorable, but too forceful and less resilient on utility/mobile work.

strengths: Strong first-viewport brand signal and memorable type scale.
Most forceful visual personality among the single skills.
Uses real motion-oriented implementation patterns.
weaknesses: Mobile typography frequently feels oversized.
Utility surfaces inherit too much dramatic marketing posture.
Several routes share similar dark-green hero language.

strengths: Tasteful, restrained, image-led hierarchy.
Strong product detail page with tangible object treatment.
Good content discipline and low filler.
weaknesses: Less adventurous than the top combinations.
Dashboard is usable but visually quiet.
Motion and interaction states are comparatively light.

strengths: Best single-skill dashboard discipline.
Strong mobile readability and practical route structures.
Good technical restraint and clean operational IA.
weaknesses: Least memorable single-skill landing page.
White/teal system repeats across surfaces.
Visual personality is precise but not especially brand-forward.

strengths: Strongest single-skill art direction.
Memorable grid-paper, object, and suite systems.
Good balance of character and prompt coverage.
weaknesses: Dashboard leans slightly editorial compared with pure operational tools.
Interaction depth is moderate rather than exceptional.
Some routes prioritize concept over maximum density.

strengths: Good original pair balance between drama and restraint.
Dashboard is clearer than GPT-Taste alone.
Product and landing pages keep strong visual anchors.
weaknesses: Suite navigation can feel cramped on mobile.
Less conceptually surprising than frontend-design pairings.
Shared beige material system risks sameness.

strengths: Design-taste improves GPT-Taste's operational discipline.
Dashboard has clearer filters, route health, and inspector structure than GPT-Taste alone.
Product page is bold but more controlled.
weaknesses: Still carries oversized GPT-Taste typography on mobile.
Less memorable than combinations that include frontend-design.
Occasional workspace-root build warnings from generated Next config.

strengths: Strong dark, expressive first impressions.
Product page feels bold and memorable.
Good visual personality.
weaknesses: Dashboard utility is weaker and a bit crowded.
Mobile type can dominate the actual workflow.
Two highly expressive skills together can over-amplify the hero posture.

strengths: Strongest pair for dashboards and practical app surfaces.
Good route/page distinction across the Northstar mini site.
Readable mobile structures and clear controls.
weaknesses: Less visually surprising than frontend-design combinations.
Landing page is competent but not top-tier memorable.
Occasional workspace-root build warnings from generated Next config.

strengths: Great pair for expressive but coherent pages.
Mechanical product page has strong object presence.
Suite pages have distinct page jobs without feeling unrelated.
weaknesses: Dashboard is a little less dense than design-taste pairings.
Some surfaces become editorial rather than workflow-first.
Motion remains moderate.

strengths: Good visual wrapper around practical UI structure.
Landing and suite pages are clean and memorable enough.
Product page has strong comparison/spec orientation.
weaknesses: Dashboard becomes too sparse compared with stronger operational runs.
Some pages favor airy composition over workflow density.
Not as distinctive as frontend-design alone on product storytelling.

strengths: Solid product/workflow coverage across all prompts.
Design-taste keeps GPT-Taste and frontend-skill from becoming too decorative.
Dashboard and suite routes feel coherent.
weaknesses: Less visually sharp than the frontend-design triples.
Beige operational system repeats across many routes.
The extra skill makes it safer, not clearly more memorable.

strengths: Best overall balance of boldness, restraint, and distinctive concept work.
Dashboard is useful without feeling generic.
Landing and product pages have strong first-viewport impact with better control than GPT-Taste alone.
weaknesses: Still has some large-type mobile pressure.
Motion is present but not the main reason it wins.
A few pages lean on similar neutral/photo materiality.

strengths: Interesting editorial character.
Strong visual mood on landing and suite pages.
Good object presence on product.
weaknesses: Often more concept-heavy than task-clear.
Mobile type and dark editorial layouts can reduce scan speed.
Dashboard is less operationally crisp than design-taste pairings.

strengths: Best no-GPT-Taste combination.
Strong practical dashboard plus distinct product/suite pages.
Keeps visual character without over-scaling or over-dramatizing.
weaknesses: Landing page is strong but not as instantly loud as GPT-Taste combinations.
Some pages use familiar beige/green product-app materiality.
Motion is restrained.

strengths: Strong broad coverage across all prompts.
Dashboard and product pages are useful and visually polished.
Shows the value of combining all skills when you need a reliable generalist.
weaknesses: All four together did not beat the best triples.
Competing guidance produces a more blended, less decisive art direction.
Some mobile pages still carry heavy hero typography.
